R.E.P.O. — A Friendships-Destroying Simulator

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 10/10 would ruin my friendships again.

R.E.P.O. is genuinely one of the most cancerous games you can play with your friends, and I mean that in the most beautiful way possible.

You load into this game thinking you're going to have a fun little gaming session with the boys, collect some valuables, make some money, and get out alive. Sounds simple enough, right? WRONG. Within 5 minutes, your entire squad has turned into a bunch of screaming idiots, someone has accidentally thrown a priceless object across the room, another guy is laughing so hard he can't breathe, and somehow I'm already ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dead.

I genuinely don't understand how I manage to die in literally every possible situation. It doesn't matter what we're doing, where we are, or how carefully I play. I could be standing in the safest corner of the map, minding my own business, and some horrific abomination from the deepest depths of hell will materialise directly behind me and send me straight to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shadow realm.

Meanwhile, my friends are somehow running around like professional exterminators, surviving things that should have killed them instantly, while I'm lying on the floor questioning every decision I've ever made in my life.

And GOD FORBID you play this game with friends who have absolutely zero brain cells.

You have one friend who thinks he's the main character and tries to fight every monster he sees. One friend who touches EVERYTHING despite being repeatedly told not to. One friend who accidentally destroys half the building while trying to carry a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lamp. And then there's the friend who laughs at everyone else's deaths but somehow becomes the biggest liability the moment something actually happens.

The worst part is that you can't even be mad at them properly because they're usually too busy laughing at your corpse to hear you screaming into the microphone.

You could be desperately begging for help while a monster is actively ripping you apart, and instead of saving you, your friends will stand 10 metres away laughing like they've just witnessed the funniest event in human history. They'll watch you get folded like a lawn chair, wait until you're completely dead, and THEN decide to ask if you need help.

THANKS, MATE. REALLY APPRECIATE THE SUPPORT.

And don't even get me started on carrying valuables. Apparently, transporting a single object from point A to point B requires the coordination of a NASA space mission. Someone bumps into a wall, the object flies across the room, the physics engine decides gravity is optional, and suddenly everyone's screaming because we've just lost more money than we made in the last three rounds.

Every single mission turns into a disaster. You start off organised, communicating, and working together like a proper team. Five minutes later, everyone is separated, the building sounds like a war zone, and I'm watching the rest of my squad from the afterlife because I somehow managed to die doing absolutely nothing.

I swear this game has a personal vendetta against me. The monsters don't even want the valuables anymore. They just want ME. They see me enter the building and immediately clock in for their shift.

My friends aren't teammates. They're unpaid funeral directors.

The amount of times I've heard my friends say, "It's fine, he's probably safe," right before I get obliterated is genuinely concerning. I could have the entire squad protecting me, and somehow the one monster we haven't seen in 20 minutes will appear out of nowhere and erase me from existence.

And the betrayal? UNFORGIVABLE.

You think you've built trust with your friends after hours of playing together. You think you know them. Then one of them decides it's a good idea to throw something at you, lure a monster into your room, or leave you behind while they escape with all the money.

Suddenly, you're not playing a co-op horror game anymore. You're participating in a psychological experiment designed to determine how quickly friendships can collapse under extreme pressure.

The funniest part is that despite all this suffering, all the screaming, all the deaths, and all the times I've threatened to uninstall the game, I STILL COME BACK FOR MORE.

Because every once in a while, you get that perfect round. Everyone's alive, the loot is valuable, the teamwork is immaculate, and you're finally convinced that maybe, just maybe, you're actually good at this game.

Then you turn around, walk into a room, and immediately ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ die.

Honestly, R.E.P.O. is an incredible game if your goal is to develop trust issues, lose your sanity, and discover which of your friends would leave you behind during an actual apocalypse.

The horror isn't the monsters. The horror is knowing that the people standing next to you are the same idiots who would sell your soul for an extra $200 worth of loot.

Final verdict:

Would I recommend this game? Absolutely.

Would I recommend playing it with friends? Only if you hate them.

Will I continue playing despite somehow being the first person to die in every single round? Unfortunately, yes.

I came here to collect valuables. I left with emotional damage, a ruined friendship, and absolutely no money.

10/10. Five stars. Someone please revive me. I'm begging you.

R.E.P.O. happens to be the best successor to Lethal Company that I have seen so far. Vanilla updates are semi-regular, the content is pretty good considering the premise and—most important of all—it is fun.

Go in, scavenge loot with your friends, don't break your loot, [b]DON'T DIE[/b], salvage value, make quota, buy upgrades and guns or vehicles, repeat.

Oh what? You don't have friends? Well, don't worry, because this game is made in a way (with the upgrade system) to allow you to play solo as well. I happen to enjoy solo gameplay, but I will tell you right now that the juice is when you play with friends.
A great game, it's fun solo, with friends and sometimes even with randoms. And it's optimized so well, it runs on my 2012 office laptop without any issue.

It's a very fun game with a good gameplay loop. Graphically, it looks pretty decent and isn't demanding at all. The audio in this game is phenomenal too.  It's a fun game to play with friends every now and then. There are some complaints I have with the game though.

For one thing, there isn't a whole lot of map variety. There's only four different map themes in total which can become a bit stale after playing for a while. There is another map theme on it's way, but I think adding some variation to the pre-existing maps would be nice too, such as switching color palettes and stuff like that. It'd also be nice if there was a bit more verticality in maps too.

The only other thing is that some monsters are really annoying in the early game when maps are smaller (the loom for example). Some of the monsters are a bit too cryptic too, I kept dying to the tick because it's gimmick of only attacking when you're holding something isn't very obvious.
